summary: This chunk is the "Request handling" section of the Ledger Service Design. It opens with one substantive request-handling claim: each request carries an idempotency key so a retried transfer does not post twice. The remaining five paragraphs are heavy repetition of about a dozen operational statements, unrelated to request handling: alert routing and paging after five minutes, low-priority backfills, a 200 ms p95 read latency target, health and readiness endpoints, unit test coverage, structured logging with request ids, a three-phase migration over two weekends, per-region dashboards, spring planning review, schema review for index impact, ninety-day secret rotation, and single-YAML-file configuration. No sentence contradicts another; the section is padded, not inconsistent.

claims.text: Each request carries an idempotency key so a retried transfer does not post twice.
Alerts route to the payments channel and page after five minutes.
Backfills run at low priority so they do not starve live traffic.
Read latency target is under 200 ms at the 95th percentile.
The service exposes health and readiness endpoints for the orchestrator.
Unit tests cover the parser, the validator, and the posting logic.
Every write path emits a structured log line with the request id.
The migration ran in three phases over two weekends without downtime.
Dashboards show throughput, error rate, and queue depth per region.
The team reviewed this design in the spring planning cycle.
Schema changes go through a review that checks index impact.
Secrets rotate every ninety days through the platform vault.
Configuration lives in a single YAML file loaded at startup.

risks.note: 200 ms p95 read latency target is stated with no measurement or source.
Five-minute paging delay is stated with no rationale or source.
Migration in three phases over two weekends without downtime is asserted with no incident data or dates.
Idempotency key is asserted but the chunk never says where the key is stored or how long duplicates are detected; the only request-handling sentence in the section.
The section repeats the same twelve sentences many times; almost none concern request handling, so the heading does not match the content.

least_confident: I could not check whether the idempotency claim on L3 is consistent with request-handling details in other chunks, since this section contains no further request-handling material.
